A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaMetrics research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial additions and relocation in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments evaluating MetaMetrics on summarization, translation, question answering, image captioning, and reward-model scoring, including component-selection and cross-dataset results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments across the five tasks and adds results for LLM-based metric combinations, alternative weighting, WMT24 evaluation, and runtime benchmarking.

M1.justification: The core Bayesian-optimization/XGBoost framework and iterative pruning algorithm remain. v3 introduces multiplicative pairwise-product and combined GP variants (Appendix C.2 and Table 15), and Table 8 changes the reported summarization XGBoost loss from reg:absoluteerror to reg:squarederror. These are limited procedural changes within the existing framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds WMT24 evaluation on English-Spanish and Japanese-Chinese (Table 18), extending coverage within translation. All five original task families remain. Hebrew-English and cross-dataset captioning were already evaluated in v1; merged summarization coverage also remains in v3's appendices.

E2.justification: v3 adds explicit Uniform and Weighted Avg ensemble comparisons for summarization, translation, QA, and reward scoring, which v1 mentioned without reporting corresponding baseline rows. It also adds UniEval and G-Eval (GPT4) as evaluated summarization comparators (Tables 1 and 9). These additions substantially strengthen the comparison set for the central calibration claim.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation design through Spearman reporting, Kendall-versus-Spearman calibration comparisons, summarization configurations with and without LLM metrics and Top-2 selection, WMT24 organizer-computed acc-t/SPA evaluation, and runtime benchmarking. It reports cleaned Skywork reward-training data and a revised summarization loss. The explicit 30/70 split description is clarification: Table 6's existing split counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test linear versus multiplicative/combined weighting (Table 15), calibration-function sensitivity (Table 16), LLM-metric inclusion and selection, runtime costs (Table 20), and summarization feature contributions (Figures 8-10). WMT24 adds unseen-language robustness evidence. The separately displayed Hebrew-English and captioning transfer tables largely repeat existing v1 results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the performance results. Both primarily present point estimates; the added correlation metrics do not change uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Summarization results are revised and expanded with LLM configurations and Spearman scores; v3 also adds ablation, runtime, and WMT24 results, including a MetaMetrics average of 0.731 in Table 18. RewardBench GP's reported overall score changes from 94.5 to 93.5, alongside changed training-data documentation, so this is not an established same-setting performance decline. Existing QA, WMT23, and captioning scores largely persist, while some oracle performance rows disappear.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly defines the multiplicative meta-metric using pairwise products and N(N-1)/2 interaction features. The existing meta-metric definition, GP assumptions, normalization equations, and kernel formulation remain substantially unchanged. No new theorem or proof appears; Appendix H mainly explains existing correlation measures.

C1.justification: The abstract, conclusion, and central contribution of flexible human-aligned calibration across five tasks remain essentially unchanged. The introduction's concrete RewardBench claim changes from outperforming the October 1 state of the art to ranking fifth of 155 overall and third on the detailed November 16 leaderboard. Some stronger superiority language nevertheless remains in the body.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting linear GP weighting to lower-dimensional optimization and identifying component inference as the runtime bottleneck, with implications for caching and parallel execution. It extends the generalization discussion to unseen languages and broadens proposed future applications. These refine the existing efficiency and robustness interpretations without replacing the paper's central explanation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the GP kernel parameter nu=2.5, benchmark CPU/GPU hardware, inference and calibration timings, and G-Eval generation settings and approximate cost. It identifies a cleaned Skywork data source and changes the stated memory ceiling from 40GB to 48GB. These materially expand reproducibility information; the repository link remains, although release wording becomes inconsistently prospective.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds an LLM-based metrics paragraph covering G-Eval, UniEval, GPT-4, T5, and MetricX-24. Additional references support the dimensionality explanation and multilingual, multicultural, code-switching, and multimodal future directions. These extend the literature context while retaining the original positioning as supervised calibration of complementary metrics.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, main section sequence, and much of the prose are retained. v3 makes targeted setup, results, and efficiency rewrites, moves limitations into Appendix A, and expands explanations of selected metrics and correlation measures. The longer appendices do not amount to a wholesale rewrite of the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns summarization tables around Kendall and Spearman columns, expands comparison tables, adds ablation and runtime tables and three summarization heatmaps, and redraws translation and reward-model weight displays. The framework diagram moves to the appendix, the leaderboard screenshot disappears, and table captions generally move above tables. Several retained results are additionally redisplayed.

improvement.justification: The added ensemble controls, UniEval/G-Eval comparisons, ablations, and measured runtime information make v3's evidence more informative and its practical costs easier to assess. However, reporting problems limit the gain: Section 5 still claims superiority over all translation baselines although Table 2 gives Weighted Avg 0.827 versus MetaMetrics XGBoost 0.825. v3 also introduces disagreement between Tables 4 and 14 for reward-model XGBoost (Iterative Best), reported as 92.9 and 92.7 respectively.
